About Keycard

At Keycard, we're building identity and access infrastructure for the agent-native era, where software isn't static but a dynamic, constantly changing system of AI agents working on behalf of people and businesses. Keycard gives every agent a verified identity and issues short-lived, task-scoped credentials at runtime, so agents can only do what they were asked to do, and every action is fully auditable. We're backed by a16z, Boldstart, and Acrew, and our founding team built and scaled Snyk, Auth0, HashiCorp, and Heroku.
The role

We're hiring a Product Manager to own how teams evaluate Keycard, and the developer experience they meet when they do.

Keycard is a control plane for agents: identity, credential exchange, delegation, policy, and audit. Every customer starts with an evaluation, and today a field engineer runs each one by hand: setup, first credential exchange, integration questions. Your job is to turn that walkthrough into product, so an evaluation can run well without us in the room.

You'll define what a successful evaluation looks like for an agent-identity product, instrument the journey so we can see where evaluators stall, then work with engineering to fix the worst spots. Sometimes the fix is a feature, more often it's a better quickstart, a template repo, an error message that says what to do next, or a docs page that assumed too much context.

Expect to spend real time with the people running evaluations: watching onboarding sessions, sitting in on field-engineering walkthroughs, reading support threads, and finding out why a team went quiet mid-eval.
What you'll do
• Own the evaluation journey end to end, from first touch through first credential exchange to a production decision, including how each stage is defined and measured.
• Set the evaluation milestones and metrics that product, engineering, and go-to-market all report against.
• Own the developer experience an evaluation runs on: SDK quickstarts, CLI onboarding, console setup, docs, and template repos.
• Drive time-to-first-credential-exchange down, and be the voice of developer ergonomics in engineering's API and CLI design discussions.
• Turn what field engineering does by hand into self-guided paths: eval guides, reference architectures, in-product guidance. Run experiments and cut the ones that don't work.
• Work with DevRel and marketing on how evaluations start, and with sales and field engineering on when a self-guided eval needs a human in the room.
What we're looking for
• You've been a PM on a developer product where evaluation and adoption were your numbers (dev tools, infrastructure, API platforms, or security).
• Technical enough to be credible with engineers. You can read an SDK quickstart and see where a developer would bounce, follow an API design discussion, and pull your own numbers in SQL or an analytics tool.
• You have taste in developer experience. You can articulate why one CLI feels good and another doesn't, and you notice error messages, defaults, and docs structure the way a designer notices spacing.
• You build with AI tools yourself and follow the agent ecosystem closely enough to have real opinions about it.
• You start from instrumentation. If the data you need doesn't exist, you get it added before forming theories about where evaluations drop off.
• Comfortable in a category with no playbook. Agent identity is new, and a lot of this job is deciding which questions are worth answering.
• You write clearly. Much of this role's output is docs, problem statements, and experiment readouts that other people act on.
Strong candidates may also have
• An engineering background before product; you've shipped code and understand what you're asking engineers to do.
• Experience productizing a high-touch motion: turning field playbooks, POC guides, or solutions-engineering work into product.
• Familiarity with identity/auth concepts (OAuth, OIDC, token exchange, delegation) or agent protocols (MCP, A2A).
• Experience with growth tooling: product analytics, experimentation frameworks, lifecycle messaging.
• Docs, quickstarts, or templates you shipped that developers actually used.
Who will love this job
• You'd rather ship a fix this week than present a strategy deck about it next month.
• You treat quickstarts and docs as product surfaces that deserve real design attention.
• You want to define the evaluation motion for a new category from scratch.
• You like being early: small team, direct access to founders and customers, no layers between you and what ships.
What We Offer
• Build at the Frontier: Work every day at the frontier of agent-native systems — shipping, inventing, and iterating on technology that hasn’t been built before. You’ll be given huge autonomy, the opportunity to gain mastery, and the chance to work in a team that holds each other accountable to succeed.
• Truly Agent-Native Culture: At Keycard, we don’t just enable others to adopt agents — we use them ourselves to build. You’ll help shape an organization that embeds AI into its foundation as an enduring competitive advantage.

• Comprehensive Benefits & Recharge: Health, dental, vision, and paramedical coverage for you and your family, plus 4 weeks vacation, 11 statutory holidays, and 1 volunteer day annually. We encourage at least 2 weeks off each year to fully recharge.

About the Role

As Senior Manager, Diagnostic & Preventive Services, you will help lead the development and execution of a portfolio strategy that expands Signify's Diagnostic & Preventive (DPS) in-home services. This is a cross-functional, hands-on role that blends analysis, existing product optimization and early-stage product development and execution. You'll work closely with teams across product, operations, clinical, and finance to identify gaps for your assigned product portfolio & create innovative solutions to improve performance as well as assess then operationalize new healthcare service concepts.

You will contribute to strategic planning while owning tactical workstreams, helping to build business cases, define product roadmaps, and support MVP launches. Your work will directly shape near-term business results and lay the groundwork for long-term growth.

Responsibilities:
• Product Strategy: You will support the development of our portfolio strategy for new in-home and virtual healthcare services, identifying and evaluating potential offerings to shape the vision and multi-year roadmap for DPS service offerings, aligning them with Signify Health's long-term business strategy.
• Problem Identification & solutioning: Deeply understand the data driving the performance of your assigned product portfolio, identifying pain points or rate limiters and collaborating with cross-functional teams to design & implement solutions, then monitor the effectiveness of the solution. You possess an innate curiosity on the 'why' and push beyond the status quo.
• Product Development: Facilitate product discovery processes, including user research, journey mapping, and pain point analysis to shape the solution design. You will translate opportunities into clear product requirements, and lead the initial launch and development of new products and service offerings.
• Market Analysis: Maintain a deep understanding of the healthcare-at-home market.Conduct market research, opportunity assessments, and competitive analysis to inform roadmap decisions and identify areas of differentiation
• Business Cases: Translate strategic opportunities into clear, data-driven business cases. Develop user experiences and journeys. Quantify value, impact, cost, and feasibility and validate product-market fit. Create prioritization frameworks to guide investment decisions. Synthesize data and insights into clear compelling recommendations.
• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate with internal stakeholders - including product, clinical, operations, finance, client success, and sales teams - to align on goals, capture feedback, and support decision-making processes.
• Product Roadmap: Support to define and maintain a 12-36 month roadmap of new service offerings that balances user needs, business objectives, and technical feasibility.
• Implementation and Go To Market: Partner cross-functionally to support implementation planning, go-to-market efforts, tracking key performance indicators, and identifying improvement opportunities.

Required Qualifications
• 7+ years of experience in product development, product management, and a mix of market and product strategy, consulting, or venture capital-preferably within healthcare.
• Familiarity with healthcare market dynamics, value-based care, and emerging models of care delivery.
• A passion for innovation and building new products that make a meaningful difference in healthcare.
• A strong mix of analytical and creative thinking, with the ability to frame problems, synthesize insights, and propose actionable solutions.
• Experience building comprehensive business cases that inform strategic investments, including market sizing, financial projections, resourcing, and scenario modeling.
• Experience in optimizing products new in market to improve performance & product profitability
• Track record of contributing to or owning parts of the product development lifecycle - from discovery through MVP and scale
• Proficiency with product development concepts and tools (e.g., JIRA, Confluence, Figma, Lucid), agile methodologies, user journeys, and product documentation.
• Strong understanding of user-centered design principles and the ability to translate insights into action.
• Comfortable analyzing data and leading discovery efforts to understand needs and validate opportunities.
• Comfortable conducting quantitative and qualitative research to evaluate feasibility, impact, and alignment with business objectives.
• Ability to distill complex information into clear business recommendations and communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Proven ability to work in cross-functional teams and drive progress across multiple workstreams.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to create clear narratives and influence stakeholders.

This position is a remote position with some travel required.
